translationRepairs: In the early Qianyuan era (758–759), Li Guangbi, Grand Preceptor, took him on as a subordinate officer. His repeated battlefield successes soon made his name known.
In the early Qianyuan era (758–759), Li Guangbi, Grand Commandant, took him on as a subordinate officer. His repeated battlefield successes soon made his name known.
太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor (太傅).

In 759 he rose from extraordinary grand censor and commanding general of the Right Imperial Guard to provisional chief minister of state ceremonials with full commissioner's standing, with overall military command at Zhengzhou as vice censor-in-chief and as regional commander over Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.

In 759 he rose from Specially Advanced and Grand General of the Right Forest Army in charge of military affairs to supernumerary Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial with regular standing, holding credentials over Zhengzhou's military affairs as prefect of Zhengzhou, acting Vice Censor-in-chief, and military governor of Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.
特進 is Specially Advanced, not a censorial title; 右羽林軍大將軍 is the Right Forest Army; 鴻臚卿員外置同正員 is a supernumerary honglu minister, not a chief minister of ceremonials framed as a censor.
At the beginning of Qianyuan, Grand Preceptor Li Guangbi brought him in as a junior commander; he repeatedly achieved merit and thereby became renowned.
At the beginning of Qianyuan, Grand Commandant Li Guangbi brought him in as a junior commander; he repeatedly achieved merit and thereby became renowned.
太尉 is Grand Commandant, not Grand Preceptor.

In the second year, from Extraordinary Grand Censor, Grand General of the Right Forest Army with knowledge of military affairs, he was promoted to Acting Commissioner-in-chief of the Court for Diplomatic Relations with the concurrent authority of a regular commissioner, holding credentials as military commissioner of Zhengzhou with concurrent post as Vice Censor-in-chief, and as military governor of the four prefectures Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.

In the second year, from Specially Advanced and Grand General of the Right Forest Army with knowledge of military affairs, he was promoted to supernumerary Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial with the standing of a regular post, holding credentials as military commissioner of Zhengzhou and concurrent prefect of Zhengzhou, acting Vice Censor-in-chief, and military governor of the four prefectures Zheng, Chen, Ying, and Bo.
特進 is Specially Advanced, not Extraordinary Grand Censor; 鴻臚卿員外置同正員 is a supernumerary honglu minister, not an acting commissioner-in-chief.
Huai'en deceived them, claiming that Ziyi had been killed by court intrigue, and led them under false pretenses.
Huai'en deceived them, claiming that Ziyi had been killed by Chao'en, and led them under false pretenses.
Chinese 朝恩 is the personal name Chao'en, not an abstract court intrigue.
Huai'en deceived the troops, saying, 'Ziyi was killed by court favoritism,' and used them by fraud.
Huai'en deceived the troops, saying, 'Ziyi was killed by Chao'en,' and used them by fraud.
Chinese 朝恩 is the personal name Chao'en, not court favoritism.
Zhu Ci had seized the capital; Li Xilie held Daliang, and Li Na rebelled at Yan.
Zhu Ci had seized the capital; Li Xilie held Daliang, and Li Na rebelled at Yun.
鄆州 is Yunzhou; Yan names a different place.
Soon the emperor withdrew to Liangzhou, and Li Huai'guang seized Hedong as well.
Soon the emperor withdrew to Liangzhou, and Li Huai'guang seized Hezhong as well.
Chinese 河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong.
Before long the emperor went to Liangzhou, and Li Huai'guang again seized Hedong by stealth.
Before long the emperor went to Liangzhou, and Li Huai'guang again seized Hezhong by stealth.
Chinese 河中 is Hezhong, not Hedong.
He died in 794 at sixty-two. Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Guardian, with graded gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain for his funeral.
He died in 794 at sixty-two. Court was suspended for three days; he was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian, with graded gifts of cloth, silk, rice, and grain for his funeral.
贈太保 is a posthumous honorary office, not an enfeoffment; enfeoffed misstates the honor.
Jian, in fear, withdrew and hastily returned the envoy's seal and the keys of office to the army supervisor.
Jian, in fear, withdrew and hastily returned the commissioner's seal and the keys of office to the army supervisor.
使印 is the command or commissioner seal Jian had taken, not the palace envoy's seal.

When Baozhen died, lieutenants including Yuan Zhongjing plotted to install his son Jian, throwing the army into turmoil. Qianxiu addressed the troops sternly: "This command belongs to the Son of Heaven. With no commander, we must await court orders — why breed sedition?"

When Baozhen died, the lieutenant Yuan Zhongjing and others discussed installing Baozhen's son Jian, throwing the army into turmoil. Qianxiu addressed the troops sternly: "Army and prefecture belong to the Son of Heaven. When the commander is absent, we must await court orders — why breed sedition?"
裨將元仲經等 is Zhongjing and other lieutenants; 軍州 is army and prefecture, not only this command.
Earlier the court musician Liu Jie had drifted to Lu; Qianxiu had him compose this piece for presentation. The present "Central Harmony Music" originated here.
Earlier the court musician Liu Jie had drifted to Luzhou; Qianxiu had him compose this piece for presentation. The present "Central Harmony Music" originated here.
Idiomatic drops 州 from 潞州, turning the prefecture Luzhou into the bare place-name Lu.
Army protector Tuhu Chenghui led Shence troops against him; Congshi often visited his camp to gamble.
Army protector Tutu Chengcui led Shence troops against him; Congshi often visited his camp to gamble.
吐突承璀 is Tutu Chengcui; Tuhu Chenghui mistransliterates both the surname 吐突 and the given name 承璀.
Congshi was greedy and acquisitive. Chenghui displayed jeweled belts and rare curios to dazzle him and gave them whenever Congshi showed delight; Congshi grew ever more intimate with him.
Congshi was greedy and acquisitive. Chengcui displayed jeweled belts and rare curios to dazzle him and gave them whenever Congshi showed delight; Congshi grew ever more intimate with him.
Chenghui should be Chengcui for 承璀, matching the correction of 吐突承璀.
The emperor adopted Pei Ji's plan: when Congshi came to gamble, Chenghui was to greet him while braves hidden in the tent seized him, bound him, loaded him into a carriage, and rushed him to court.
The emperor adopted Pei Ji's plan: when Congshi came to gamble, Chengcui was to greet him while braves hidden in the tent seized him, bound him, loaded him into a carriage, and rushed him to court.
Chenghui should be Chengcui for 承璀.
His sons Jizong and the other four men were all demoted beyond the Ling mountains.
His sons Jizong and the other three men, four in all, were all demoted beyond the Ling mountains.
子繼宗等四人 means Jizong together with others totaling four, not Jizong plus four more.

Upon leaving office robes he was recorder of Shanggui, was thrice promoted to probationary appraiser of the Court of Judicial Review, and acted as Investigating Censor and supply commissioner of the Shannan East circuit observation mission.

Upon leaving commoner's clothes (taking his first office) he was recorder of Shanggui, was thrice promoted to probationary appraiser of the Court of Judicial Review, and acted as Investigating Censor and supply commissioner of the Shannan East circuit observation mission.
解褐 is assuming office for the first time, not leaving office robes; the literal reverses the idiom.

A year later he became deputy to Lu Sigong, was made acting left subordinate heir apparent and military governor of Heyang and Huai, with five eastern capital counties including Si added to his jurisdiction.

A year later he became deputy to Lu Sigong, was made Acting Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and military governor of Heyang and Huai, with five eastern capital counties including Si added to his jurisdiction.
左庶子 is the Left Mentor (shuzi) of the heir apparent, not a 'left subordinate heir apparent'.

After a year he became deputy to the military governor Lu Sigong, was given the additional posts of Acting Left Subordinate Heir Apparent and military governor and observation commissioner of the three Heyang cities and Huaizhou, with five counties including Sishui of the eastern capital circuit placed under his jurisdiction.

After a year he became deputy to the military governor Lu Sigong, was given the additional posts of Acting Left Mentor of the Heir Apparent and military governor and observation commissioner of the three Heyang cities and Huaizhou, with five counties including Sishui of the eastern capital circuit placed under his jurisdiction.
The literal rendering repeats the same office mistranslation of 左庶子.
Advancing to besiege Yue at Weizhou, the general Fu Lin came over by night with five hundred elite horsemen; Peng opened the camp at his ear to receive them.
Advancing to besiege Yue at Weizhou, the general Fu Lin came over by night with five hundred elite horsemen; Peng then opened the camp to receive them.
耳 is a modal particle (or a graphic error for 亟/乃), not the anatomical ear; 'opened the camp at his ear' is a false literalism.

He died in 786 at fifty-four. Court was suspended for one day; he was posthumously made Minister of Works, with graded gifts of cloth, silk, and grain. Gui Jingchong, left regular attendant, was sent as mourning envoy, and all funeral costs were paid by the state.

He died in 786 at fifty-four. Court was suspended for one day; he was posthumously made Minister of Works, with graded gifts of cloth, silk, and grain. Gui Chongjing, left regular attendant, was sent as mourning envoy, and all funeral costs were paid by the state.
歸崇敬 is Gui Chongjing; the English name reverses the given-name syllables as Jingchong.

In the second year he died at age fifty-four. Court was suspended for one day; he was posthumously given Minister of Works. Funeral gifts of cloth, silk, and grain were given in graded amounts, and the Left Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat Gui Jingchong was ordered to serve as mourning envoy; all funeral expenses along the route were commanded to be supplied by the state.

In the second year he died at age fifty-four. Court was suspended for one day; he was posthumously given Minister of Works. Funeral gifts of cloth, silk, and grain were given in graded amounts, and the Left Regular Attendant at the Imperial Secretariat Gui Chongjing was ordered to serve as mourning envoy; all funeral expenses along the route were commanded to be supplied by the state.
The literal English likewise reverses 崇敬 as Jingchong instead of Chongjing.
